emitted mechanically from one catalog entry (★★ EMITTER SUBSTRATE —
*every repeating impl is a spec; emit, don't author*). This table is a
generated mirror of the catalog: it is regenerated, never edited, so it
can never drift from what is actually published.

## Adopting these across a crate

Don't hand-write `#[derive(...)]` site-by-site — let the survey find and
apply them:

```bash
# what could this crate adopt?
tatara-rust-forge survey <crate-src-path>
# apply every candidate atomically (rolls back if the cargo gate goes red)
tatara-rust-forge survey-apply-all <crate-root> --write
```

## Is more farming worth it?

The diminishing-returns metric scores the whole fleet and tells you
whether to keep adopting or to stop:

```bash
tatara-rust-forge survey-fleet-returns <org-root>
```

A `Plateau` verdict means the mechanical-impl toil has been harvested —
stop refactoring and let new code consume the derives as it is written.
